package_info.why_malicious: The report summarizes multiple high-profile malware and ransomware campaigns (Conti, BlackCat, Clop, Cheers, ERMAC, ChromeLoader, Cobalt Strike) but does not provide any specific package-based malware or code snippets. Instead, it describes attack campaigns, ransomware operations, and vulnerabilities exploited in the wild. No individual software package or codebase is identified as the source of malicious code.

behavioral_signatures: Ransomware encrypting large numbers of endpoints and demanding ransom
Credential theft and exfiltration from mobile banking apps
Browser hijacking and redirection to advertising sites
Phishing emails delivering RATs disguised as Windows updates
Fake proof-of-concept exploits delivering Cobalt Strike beacons
file_indicators: Browser extensions or scripts injected by ChromeLoader
Proof-of-concept exploit files with embedded backdoors
network_indicators: Redirection to advertising or affiliate marketing sites
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for ransomware-specific file encryption patterns, unauthorized credential access on mobile devices, browser extension or script injection, suspicious outbound network connections to known C2 or affiliate domains, and execution of files masquerading as legitimate updates or proof-of-concept exploits. Use endpoint protection, network monitoring, and threat intelligence feeds to correlate indicators.
